topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session, connects it to histopathology practicals, and outlines the learning outcomes for cancer genetics and transformation.

topics.label: Viral Origins of Oncogenes and Assays for Cellular Transformation
topics.groupedBecause: The study of tumor viruses revealed that cancer arises from altered cellular genes, whose ability to drive oncogenesis can be evaluated using cell culture and animal assays.

topics.label: Functional Classification and Mechanisms of Oncogenes and Tumor Suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: Oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes are defined by whether mutations cause dominant gains or recessive losses of function, as exemplified by cell cycle regulation and dominant-negative mechanisms.

topics.label: Mechanisms, Consequences, and Dynamics of Genetic Instability
topics.groupedBecause: Defects in DNA repair, replication, and mitotic chromosome segregation generate genetic instability that accelerates the stepwise accumulation of mutations driving tumor progression.

topics.label: Hereditary Cancer Predisposition and Tumor Evolution
topics.groupedBecause: Inherited mutations in caretaker and gatekeeper genes accelerate cancer development, while subsequent tumor evolution can bypass the need for continued genetic instability.

topics.label: Conclusion and Recommended Reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session, offers recommended reading on the history of cancer research, and previews the next lecture on cancer hallmarks.
